I answered this from a read-only look at the file and changed nothing. I didn't run the git status, git log or GSD progress checks from the hand-off card.

In `tools/verified_reuse.py`, after the vendored `decideReuse` call returns a hit (`v.get("hit")` is truthy), `lookup()` refuses it at line 170 with the check `if v.get("accepted") is not False or v.get("needsFreshReview") is not True:`. When that holds, it returns the constant **`REFUSED`** with `{"reason": "reuse result claimed acceptance; a cache cannot approve"}` (line 173). So a hit is refused unless it comes back marked `accepted` exactly `False` and `needsFreshReview` exactly `True`. The comment above it explains why: "The vendored contract is that a hit is never an approval. If that ever changes upstream, refuse rather than pass an approval through a cache." A refused hit is also never written to the log as a `"hit"` event.

foreign-repo-key:baseline.text:
The namespaced key is built at `tools/plan_graph_check.py:121`: `p = f"[repo-{hashlib.sha1(ident.encode()).hexdigest()[:10]}]/{p}"`. The hash function is **SHA-1** (`hashlib.sha1`), and the key keeps only the first 10 hex characters of the digest. The input `ident` comes from the line before it (line 120): `ident = os.path.normcase(str(_common_repo(root) or root))`. That is the other repository's common git directory, or its work-tree root if there isn't one, with case folded by `normcase`. The whole branch only runs when `_common_repo(root) != home` (line 117). So files in worktrees of this same repository keep plain relative paths, and a file in a different repository, including a submodule, gets a `[repo-<sha1[:10]>]/` prefix. The comment on line 118 says the prefix is there so a key never carries a home directory.

I didn't edit, create or delete any file.
